answer: An orchard of agent identities gets priced like a fresh AMM pool: each new sybil must post bonded liquidity that deepens with every mint, so faking uniqueness costs real capital at the margin. A lagoon of shallow fake pools gets arbitraged away because the bonding curve steepens quadratically, forcing attackers to lock escalating collateral per identity until marginal cost exceeds marginal sybil payoff. The haven limit is capital efficiency: wealthy attackers can still rent depth across pools, so bonding alone caps but never eliminates sybils without slashing or reputation overlays.
